scope: Single-node DT BF16 and FP8 use fixed M64 for every token count; PF geometry is unchanged.
parity: tests/torchrun_pf_dt.py compares training=True PF retaining backward state against inference DT, with strict BF16 storage-bit equality. Every PF tape is consumed by backward and all gradients must be finite. Normal and compact FP8 workspaces are covered.
routing: Distributed distinct experts, or all tokens routed to two distinct experts on one destination rank. Training rejects duplicate experts within a token, so inference-only duplicate-routing cases belong in the DT suite.
shapes: Three model dimensions; 16 experts, top-k 2; tokens/rank 1,2,4,8,16,32,63,64,65,127,128,129,256,512 plus unequal lengths with rank0 empty.
performance: EP8 slowest-rank CUDA-event graph-replay times; source FP8 online quantization included; weight preparation excluded. Formal 256-expert model shapes; tokens/rank 1,16,32,64,128,256,512.
history: The obsolete automatic-M autotune worker was stopped. Old immutable binaries, source snapshots and measurement reports are retained as evidence, not active implementation. No M dimension is left in the active tuner.
result: Final fixed-M64 binaries: 3600/3600 training-PF/DT rank-cases match exactly, including normal and compact FP8 workspaces. Each PF tape consumed by backward. Full DT and paired performance results are in docs/benchmarks/dt_m64_20261101.json.
